title: The AI Vibeshift
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Dave Stuart Jr., a high school teacher, reports a shift in his students' attitudes toward AI this school year: a student panel asked staff to stop using AI to produce learning materials, students groaned at AI-generated images in a video, and some were dismayed by AI-made locker signs. He treats this as part of a wider souring on AI. He doubts the shift stops students from using AI to dodge effortful homework, and he judges AI use by whether it harms growth toward mastery. His main practical claim is that students who perceive a teacher's AI use will count it against the teacher's credibility, the base of his Five Key Beliefs for motivation. He offers teachers questions about disclosure, justification and simplifying work before turning to AI, and asks whether there is any 'good' student or teacher AI use.
points: Stuart notices students becoming more negative about AI, and points to a student panel, AI-generated art that students spotted before he did, and wider public backlash as evidence.
A negative attitude does not necessarily stop students from using AI to avoid time-intensive busywork.
The test he applies to student AI use is whether it harms growth toward mastery and long-term flourishing.

Student-facing AI products from teachers risk eroding credibility, the foundation of his Five Key Beliefs about student motivation, so teachers should expect to justify any such use to a skeptical audience.
He suggests teachers ask whether they would disclose AI use, why not if they would not, and whether simplifying the work would be better than automating it.
quotes: Is it just me, or have high school students undergone a vibeshift toward AI this school year?

a student shared that one thing our school could improve would be teachers and staff not using AI to produce learning materials for students; she said this makes it harder to respect the staff at the school.
The goal is always helping student to grow toward mastery because this is the most efficient and role-appropriate avenue for me as a teacher to advance their long-term flourishing.
It is highly likely that students who perceive that a teacher or staff member has used AI will internalize this as a drain on Credibility.
I think it’s wrong to assume that using AI for student-facing products is going to have a neutral effect on Credibility.
Instead of using AI to manage my impossible workload, how could I instead kist make the work I’m trying to get done simpler?
what’s happening to ME when I use this technology? The short-term benefits appear obvious but… what about in the long-term?
